- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for high sentiment periods.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), especially if sentiment peaks; apply a 2–5 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply a downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid shifts >0.3), model exhibits erratic behavior; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values to reduce noise.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75–77), model tends to hold too high; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days after peak.
